theory.intro: Simplifying a rate means writing it as a **unit rate** — a rate whose second quantity is $1$. Write the two quantities as a fraction with their units, divide both by the denominator, then rewrite the answer using a slash. The unit rate answers 'how much for each one?'.
facts: A **unit rate** has $1$ as its second quantity: $\$7$/kg means $\$7$ for each $1$ kg.
Dividing the numerator and the denominator by the denominator makes the denominator $1$: $\frac{150\text{ beats}}{3\text{ min}}=\frac{50\text{ beats}}{1\text{ min}}$.
The units of the answer come from the units of the fraction: money over mass gives $\$$/kg, distance over time gives km/h.
Which quantity goes on top matters: from $216$ km on $24$ L you can write $9$ km/L or $\frac{1}{9}$ L/km, and the two are reciprocals.
When the division does not come out exactly, round sensibly — money to the nearest cent, other rates usually to $2$ decimal places.
steps: Write the rate as a fraction with units.
Divide the numerator and the denominator by the denominator.
Rewrite the simplified rate using a slash.

foundation.question_text: Simplify to a unit rate: $\$45$ for $9$ kg.
Simplify to a unit rate: $240$ km in $3$ hours.
Simplify to a unit rate: $15$ goals in $3$ games.
Simplify to a unit rate: $\$17.50$ for every $5$ kg.
Simplify to a unit rate: $36\,000$ cans in $8$ hours.
Simplify to a unit rate: $80$ mm of rain in $5$ days.
Simplify to a unit rate: $\$10$ for $2.5$ kg.
Simplify to a unit rate: $15$ km in $60$ minutes.

development.question_text: Simplify to a unit rate, correct to the nearest cent: $\$160$ for $6$ hours.
A car travels $243$ km using $30$ litres of petrol. Express this as a simplified rate in km/L.
A lift should carry no more than $1600$ kg or $20$ people. Write this weight allowance as a rate in kg/person.
$53$ litres of petrol cost $\$73.67$. Express this cost as a rate in $\$$/L, correct to the nearest cent.
$30$ salad rolls were bought to feed $20$ people, at a total cost of $\$120$. Find the unit rate for rolls per person, and the unit rate for cost per roll.
development.solution_text:
$\frac{30\text{ rolls}}{20\text{ people}}$
$=\frac{1.5\text{ rolls}}{1\text{ person}}$
$=1.5\text{ rolls/person}$
$\frac{\$120}{30\text{ rolls}}$
$=\frac{\$4}{1\text{ roll}}$
$=\$4\text{/roll}$

development.question_text: A car uses $24$ L of petrol to travel $216$ km. Express these quantities as a simplified rate in kilometres per litre, and again in litres per kilometre.
development.solution_text:
$\frac{216\text{ km}}{24\text{ L}}$
$=\frac{9\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}$
$=9\text{ km/L}$
$\frac{24\text{ L}}{216\text{ km}}$
$=\frac{\frac{1}{9}\text{ L}}{1\text{ km}}$
$=\frac{1}{9}\text{ L/km}$

development.question_text: Dr Rosanna starts seeing patients at $8{:}30$ am and finishes at $5{:}30$ pm. She saw $40$ patients. Find the rate at which she saw patients, in patients/hour, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
$8{:}30$ am to $5{:}30$ pm is $9$ hours.
$\frac{40\text{ patients}}{9\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{4.444\ldots\text{ patients}}{1\text{ h}}$
$=4.44\text{ patients/h}$

mastery.question_text: Tom was $120$ cm tall when he turned $10$ years old and $185$ cm tall when he turned $20$ years old. Find Tom's average rate of growth per year over that time.
mastery.solution_text:
$185-120=65$ cm of growth
$20-10=10$ years
$\frac{65\text{ cm}}{10\text{ years}}$
$=\frac{6.5\text{ cm}}{1\text{ year}}$
$=6.5\text{ cm/year}$

mastery.question_text: The Burwood Football Club had $12\,000$ members. After five successful years it now has $18\,000$ members. Find the average rate of membership growth per year.
mastery.solution_text:
$18\,000-12\,000=6000$ new members
$\frac{6000\text{ members}}{5\text{ years}}$
$=\frac{1200\text{ members}}{1\text{ year}}$
$=1200\text{ members/year}$

mastery.question_text: A car had a full tank of $56$ L at the start of a $75$ km journey. At the end of the journey the tank was three quarters full. Find the fuel consumption rate in kilometres per litre, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
$\frac{3}{4}\times56=42$ L left in the tank
$56-42=14$ L used
$\frac{75\text{ km}}{14\text{ L}}$
$=\frac{5.357\ldots\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}$
$=5.36\text{ km/L}$
